keyFindings.text: **minIterations is a lower bound only, and it is research-only.** It applies only when `loopType === 'research' && minIterations > 1`, and the shipped research default is 3. Once it clears it does nothing to extend depth. The review loop has no minIterations floor in `convergence.cjs`, and `deep-review.yaml` never mentions one. Review can stop as early as its rolling-average signal (2 ratios) plus the coverage vote allow. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/convergence.cjs:1159] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research.yaml:550] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/convergence.cjs:775] [INFERENCE: an empty grep for minIterations in .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-review.yaml]

**newInfoRatio is a self-reported, focus-relative number.** The ratios come straight from the agent's iteration records, filtered only by status. The agent contract scores novelty per finding of the current focus. Deep drilling on one sub-question naturally produces falling ratios, and a rolling average under 0.05 counts as a stop vote. The only cross-check is a novelty-corroboration guard, which blocks STOP only when the reported novelty is low AND graph novelty is above its floor. It can veto a stop, but it can never add scope. The recorded defect is only half right.** An explicit `--claude-config-dir` on a research run is not silently ignored: `validateFlags` rejects it with the UsageError "flag '--claude-config-dir' is only valid with --executor cli-claude-code --loop-type review". The silent path is the environment: only the review branch builds `parentEnv` with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and passes `guardContext: { env: parentEnv }`. **Research progress is measured against a question set fixed at init.** `totalQuestions` is just `answeredCount + openCount` from the findings registry. A STOP candidate (`all_questions_answered`) exists as soon as every registered question is answered, and it skips the weighted vote. Nothing in the stop path counts unexplored scope, so a loop that answers its 3-5 init questions narrowly has done everything the stop logic can see. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/convergence.cjs:1415] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/convergence.cjs:1149]

**The focusAlignment quality guard actively penalizes widening.** It fails when any iteration answers a question that is not in that iteration's own `keyQuestions` list, which turns a STOP candidate into CONTINUE (`qualityGuardFailed`). Today that is harmless, but it means an iteration answering an emergent question is booked as a violation rather than as scope growth. An expansive mode must either register the new question first or exempt frontier-born questions from the guard. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/convergence.cjs:880] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/convergence.cjs:1168]

**The graph decision can block a stop but cannot widen.** `STOP_ALLOWED` requires every trace entry to pass: questionCoverage >= 0.7, claimVerificationRate >= 0.6, contradictionDensity <= 0.15, sourceDiversity >= 1.5 and evidenceDepth >= 1.5. All five are ratios over the existing QUESTION/FINDING/SOURCE nodes, and none measures unvisited frontier nodes. A missing graph decision yields CONTINUE (`graphDecisionMissing`), so the graph is a veto layer over the question set, not a frontier. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/convergence.cjs:432] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/convergence.cjs:1799] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/convergence.cjs:1004]

**The only built-in ways to run longer are blunt.** `convergenceMode: off` and `stopPolicy: max-iterations` turn the vote into telemetry and run to the cap. They extend duration, not direction, so the loop still works the same fixed question set. Their real breadth effect belongs to Q3. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/convergence.cjs:1138] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research.yaml:963]

**The sourceDiversity guard deepens evidence per question, not the scope.** It requires at least 2 cited SOURCE nodes per answered question. That is depth along an existing question, never breadth. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/convergence.cjs:864]

**The stop order is fixed and the script owns it.** First match wins: max-iterations cap, 3 consecutive failures, stuck threshold, convergence-mode `off`, stop-policy `max-iterations`, then a STOP candidate, then the minIterations floor, then quality guards, then the graph decision. The YAML only branches on the result and never recomputes it. **The stuck path recovers but never widens.** A ratio below threshold increments `stuckCount`, and an `insight` status resets it. Reaching `stuckThreshold` gives STUCK_RECOVERY, not a scope expansion. How recovery chooses its new focus belongs to Q2. **The weighted vote rewards answering the known questions, not finding new ones.** The research vote has three signals: rolling average of the last 3 newInfoRatios below the threshold (weight 0.30), the MAD noise floor (0.35, needs 4 ratios), and `questionEntropy`, the answered fraction, at or above 0.85 (0.35). Unavailable signals drop out of the denominator. So in iterations 1-2, `questionEntropy` alone carries the vote: 6 of 7 answered gives a score of 1.0, which is above 0.60. **`research/inbox.jsonl` is the only path that grows the canonical question set, and nothing in the runtime writes to it.** The reducer reads the inbox on every reduce step and merges its rows into the registry. Those rows do count toward `totalQuestions`. But no runtime script or YAML writes the inbox. Outside docs, tests and the trigger index, `inbox.jsonl` appears only in `reduce-state.cjs`. The `angle-bank` origin exists only as an enum value in the reducer. An operator or an analyst has to append rows by hand.
**A question can be resolved by a matching focus string, and the matching is literal.** A question counts as resolved when one of three things holds:

**An ambient `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` still reaches the research child.** The research branch passes no `guardContext`. `runAuditedExecutorCommand` therefore builds the child env from `process.env`. `buildExecutorDispatchEnv` keeps every key that passes `isAllowedExecutorEnvKey`, and `CLAUDE_` is an allowed prefix for `cli-claude-code`. So the child silently uses whichever account the parent shell has, not the one the operator configured.

**Carried-forward questions steer focus but never enter the stop denominator.** `buildCarriedForwardOpenQuestions` collects every free-text item under an iteration's `Questions Remaining` heading, and every `openQuestions` or `questionsRemaining` value on a record, that does not match an open registry question. These items are kept separately as `carriedForwardOpenQuestions`. The registry's `keyedQuestions`, `openQuestions` and `metrics.openQuestions` are built only from the strategy and inbox questions. So an emergent question can become the next focus, but it never raises `totalQuestions`, and it can never block `all_questions_answered` or lower `questionEntropy` (iteration-1 findings 2-3).

**Fan-out is not affected.** `fanout-run.cjs` checks `lineage.configDir` for any `cli-claude-code` lineage, with no loop-type condition, and injects `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` into the spawned lineage's env after the allowlist filter. It does not call `dispatch-iteration.cjs`. The blast radius is single-lineage `/deep:research` runs with `--executor=cli-claude-code --config-dir=...`. Whether a fan-out lineage's own iterations later re-dispatch through `dispatch-iteration.cjs` is not verified (inference).
